text:
ConocoPhillips fell 1.8% today as oil prices dropped following diplomatic talks between the U.S. and Iran at the UN. When crude prices decline, they directly reduce revenue and profit margins for oil producers like ConocoPhillips—and the prospect of a negotiated resolution to Middle East tensions removes some of the geopolitical risk premium that has been supporting oil prices. The stock is now down 7.2% over two weeks as this uncertainty has weighed on the sector.

The broader backdrop adds to the pressure: the Trump administration is considering a diesel export ban to address domestic fuel costs ahead of midterm elections, which could further constrain refining margins and oil demand. Crude prices remain volatile with no clear direction—U.S. oil at $107/barrel versus global crude at $130/barrel shows the market is conflicted on both supply and geopolitical risk.
